name: DeepMind Control Suite
ability_definition: The ability to coordinate the movement of your arms, legs, and torso together when the whole body is in motion.

task_realism.reasoning: Humanoid stand, walk and run require coordinating many joints across legs, torso and arms while the whole body moves, so they touch the core of the ability. Real workplace uses are different, though: climbing ladders, carrying loads, moving over uneven terrain, fighting fires, construction, and athletic or rescue work. These involve contact with objects and environments. The benchmark offers only flat-ground locomotion with a simplified 21-joint body in idealized physics, with no load carrying, obstacles or purposeful whole-body work.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: Evaluation happens in a deterministic MuJoCo simulation with clean proprioceptive state or rendered pixels. There is no sensor noise, actuator wear or terrain variation. Episodes reset freely, and falls cost nothing. The cited result used a very large training budget (roughly 1e8 steps). Real work involves one-shot physical execution, safety stakes, fatigue, unstructured and changing environments, and little tolerance for trial and error. The sim-to-real gap is large.

construct_coverage.reasoning: The reward measures horizontal speed and staying upright, not the quality or efficiency of coordination. Degenerate gaits such as running backwards or sideways, or odd limb use, still count as solutions, so arm-torso-leg integration is rewarded only indirectly. Several aspects are missing: coordination while manipulating objects, balance recovery under perturbation, transitions between different movements, and adapting to terrain. Locomotion is only a narrow slice of gross body coordination.

format_match.reasoning: The agent sends continuous joint torques and receives a scalar return on a 0-1000 scale. This resembles low-level control of a real legged robot, but real work is judged by getting physical tasks done safely, not by speed-upright reward in a simplified body model. No real work artifacts or outcomes are produced.

transferability_reasoning: DMC humanoid-run is a clean, standardized test of multi-joint whole-body locomotion control, which is a genuine but narrow component of Gross Body Coordination. Several factors separate it from real workplace coordination: simulated idealized physics, a reward that ignores coordination quality and allows odd gaits, no object interaction or environmental variability, and huge trial-and-error training budgets. Transfer is therefore weak.

2020.metric: mean episode return on humanoid:run (0-1000 scale)
2020.human_reference: General adult population. Gross body coordination for walking and running is a general ability, not a specialist one.

2021.human_reference: General adult workforce. Gross body coordination (running, balance recovery, whole-body movement) is a broadly held ability, and most workers performing physical tasks have it at a basic level.

2022.human_reference: General adult workforce performing whole-body motor tasks (walking, running, lifting, climbing, balancing while moving), e.g., manual and physical-labor workers
